label: late original-phase steps / first copy step in sequences starting with t, c, or 1 (highly conjunctive, low precision)
explanation: Sparse feature (about 0.04% of steps). Activity is concentrated on original-phase steps at position 4 or later (about 70% of mass, more in longer sequences, L 8-9) and on the first copy step (recall_idx 1, where the input is the first token, about 27% of mass). It almost never fires at t<3 or deep in the copy phase. Activity depends strongly on the first token: t gives 13.7x lift and 47% of mass, with c, 1, and v weaker. The input token (q, v, w, c, n), the previous token (r, j, a, g, o, p), and an e at position 2 or 3 also raise the rate. The predicate built from first token plus position covers about 76% of activation mass, but its precision is only about 1%: most steps that match it are inactive. Adding token conditions raises precision only to about 15% and drops recall to about 12%. So the feature reads a specific conjunction of sequence history that simple predicates do not capture. Activation magnitude is small and narrow (median 0.13, max 0.29). Magnitude modulation was not characterized beyond a slight rise in coverage for higher-activation quartiles.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=t (+5.57), orig0=c (+4.14), orig0=1 (+4.11), orig1=t (+3.74), orig2=e (+3.50), recall_idx=1 (+3.49). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-5.38), orig4=- (-3.73), prev_tok=e (-3.62), orig3=1 (-3.09).
